lines.cap: Pirates almost never buried their booty.
lines.say: Pirates almost never buried their booty.

lines.cap: X marks the spot. A chest of gold, buried on a desert island.
lines.say: X marks the spot. A chest of gold, buried on a desert island.

lines.cap: Real pirates? They spent it. Fast. On food, drink and partying in port.
lines.say: Real pirates? They spent it. Fast. On food, drink and partying in port.

lines.cap: The loot was split between the whole crew, often right after the raid.
lines.say: The loot was split between the whole crew, often right after the raid.

lines.cap: There's really only one famous case. In 1699, Captain William Kidd buried some treasure on an island near New York.
lines.say: There's really only one famous case. In 1699, Captain William Kidd buried some treasure on an island near New York.

lines.cap: It was dug up and used as evidence against him. He was hanged in 1701.
lines.say: It was dug up and used as evidence against him. He was hanged in 1701.

lines.cap: The X on the map? Mostly from a novel. Treasure Island, published in 1883.
lines.say: The X on the map? Mostly from a novel. Treasure Island, published in 1883.

lines.cap: So pirates didn't bury their booty. They shook it.
lines.say: So pirates didn't bury their booty. They shook it.
